The international lines of credit generally are renewable on an annual basis and certain facilities are fully and unconditionally guaranteed by Wesco Distribution, Inc. (“Wesco Distribution”). The applicable interest rate for borrowings under these lines of credit varies by country and is governed by the applicable loan agreement. In addition to the results provided in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“U.S. GAAP”), our discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations includes certain non-GAAP financial measures, which are defined further below. These financial measures include organic sales growth, earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (“EBITDA”), adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA margin, financial leverage, adjusted selling, general and administrative expenses, adjusted income from operations, adjusted other non-operating expense (income), adjusted provision for income taxes, adjusted income before income taxes, adjusted net income, adjusted net income attributable to WESCO International, Inc., adjusted net income attributable to common stockholders, and adjusted earnings per diluted share. We believe that these non-GAAP measures are helpful to users of our financial statements as they provide a better understanding of our financial condition and results of operations on a comparable basis. Additionally, certain non-GAAP measures either focus on or exclude items impacting comparability of results, allowing users to more easily compare our financial performance from period to period. Management uses certain non-GAAP financial measures in its evaluation of the performance of the Company’s operating segments and in the determination of incentive compensation. Management does not use these non-GAAP financial measures for any purpose other than the reasons stated above. We employ approximately 21,000 people, maintain relationships with more than 35,000 suppliers, and serve nearly 130,000 customers worldwide. With millions of products, end-to-end supply chain services and significant digital capabilities, Wesco provides innovative solutions to meet customer needs across commercial and industrial businesses, technology companies, telecommunications providers, and utilities. Our innovative solutions include supply chain management, logistics and transportation, procurement, warehousing and inventory management, as well as kitting and labeling, limited assembly of products and installation enhancement. Wesco operates more than 700 sites, including distribution centers, fulfillment centers and sales offices in approximately 50 countries, providing a local presence for customers and a global network to serve multi-location businesses and global corporations. credit_strengths.text: Wesco's scale as a business-to-business distribution and supply chain franchise across electrical, communications and utility segments underpins a diversified revenue base, and operating income remains positive despite margin compression, supporting the view that the core franchise generates earnings through the cycle.

Liquidity is a clear relative strength: the current ratio sits well above the sector median and comfortably above one, with working capital funded by receivables securitization and revolver capacity, giving the issuer meaningful headroom to absorb seasonal inventory swings.

key_risks.text: Gross leverage sits above the sector median and rose year over year, with net leverage also above the sector median and above prior year, placing the indicative financial risk profile in the highly leveraged band and leaving only modest headroom to the next risk boundary.

The debt note shows a large receivables securitization facility and revolver borrowings alongside senior notes maturing in the near and medium term, so refinancing and facility renewal risk is concentrated rather than spread; the securitization is a structural funding dependence worth monitoring.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is below both the sector median and prior year, and EBITDA coverage is similarly weaker than the sector, indicating debt service consumes a comparatively large share of earnings; the cash interest proxy is the only available interest measure, so coverage is approximate.

Operating cash flow fell sharply year over year and falls short of dividends plus buybacks combined, while free cash flow is far below distributions and negligible against debt, so shareholder returns are effectively funded from balance sheet capacity rather than internally generated cash.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative profile is highly leveraged, driven by weak cash flow relative to debt rather than by earnings alone; leverage is above the sector median and trending higher, and cash conversion deteriorated materially, so the credit trajectory is negative absent a working capital recovery.

Our judgement is that liquidity and the safe-zone distress score provide a cushion, but thin free cash flow against a meaningful distribution programme and concentrated maturities means the issuer depends on refinancing access; we would monitor cash generation and facility renewals closely.

credit_strengths.text: Wesco作為橫跨電氣、通訊及公用事業分部的企業對企業分銷及供應鏈業務的特許經營權，其規模支撐了多元化的收入基礎，且儘管利潤率受壓，經營收入仍保持正數，支持核心特許經營權在整個週期內產生盈利的觀點。
流動性是明顯的相對優勢：流動比率遠高於行業中位數，並穩健地高於一，營運資金由應收賬款證券化及循環信貸額度提供資金，使發行人擁有可觀的緩衝空間以吸收季節性存貨波動。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿高於行業中位數並按年上升，淨槓桿亦高於行業中位數及高於上年，使指示性財務風險狀況處於高槓桿區間，距下一風險界限僅餘有限緩衝空間。
債務附註顯示存在大型應收賬款證券化融資及循環信貸借款，同時有於近期及中期到期的優先票據，故再融資及融資額度續期風險集中而非分散；該證券化屬結構性融資依賴，值得監察。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率低於行業中位數及上年水平，EBITDA覆蓋率同樣較行業為弱，顯示償債佔盈利的比重相對較大；現金利息代理指標為唯一可得的利息衡量，故覆蓋率屬約略估算。
經營現金流按年大幅下降，並不足以覆蓋股息加回購的總和，而自由現金流遠低於分派且相對債務微不足道，故股東回報實際上由資產負債表能力而非內部產生現金提供資金。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性狀況為高槓桿，驅動因素為現金流相對債務疲弱而非僅因盈利；槓桿高於行業中位數並呈上升趨勢，現金轉換顯著惡化，故在營運資金未復甦的情況下，信貸軌跡為負面。
我們的判斷是流動性及安全區困境評分提供緩衝，但相對於可觀的分派計劃及集中的到期債務，自由現金流薄弱，意味發行人依賴再融資渠道；我們會密切監察現金產生及融資額度續期。
